headline: Highest risk is compliance/data leakage from social-auto-upload’s broad egress and file/API handling; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by godot_rl_agents’ no-egress, non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and social-auto-upload, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of outputs into social-auto-upload’s CLI/file inputs, which is an unusual configuration and not a default interaction. Uncertainty remains because the pairwise bridge is undocumented, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies godot_rl_agents output into social-auto-upload CLI arguments or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into social-auto-upload commands.
Use a human review step before any upload action.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared mount.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data and files and has broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents is documented with no network egress. If outputs from the game agent are fed into the uploader, the uploader can transmit that content to third-party platforms/APIs. The pairwise leakage path is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are stored in files that social-auto-upload reads, those contents can be uploaded.
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at sensitive media or account files, those data classes may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of social-auto-upload inputs.
Use a staging directory with only approved media.
Review upload targets before running.
Rotate or scope account credentials narrowly.
requires-engineering: add allowlists for upload destinations and file paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents exposes no write or shell capabilities in the profile, and social-auto-upload explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell execution, and subprocess spawning. With no overlapping mutable write surface documented, a direct capability conflict is not plausible. The absence of write surfaces in both profiles blocks the rubric’s conflict pathways.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted shared filesystem write or git mutation, conflict risk changes.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared mutable state, the pathway may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Do not grant shared write access to the same directory.
Avoid running them under the same mutable account file.
Use separate processes and directories.
requires-engineering: add explicit locking for any future shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: social-auto-upload can act on files and APIs, so if it consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative instructions or metadata, errors can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing agent, so its outputs are not inherently verified facts. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is used as upload metadata without verification, wrong content can be published.
IF social-auto-upload treats upstream text as authoritative, cascading errors can reach external platforms.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before upload.
Validate filenames, captions, and targets against a checklist.
Use dry-run mode if available.
Separate generation from publication.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for upstream outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media to external platforms, creating retention and residency concerns; godot_rl_agents is open-source and non-runnable, so it is not the compliance driver here. Because the pair can move account/media data into third-party services, but no specific residency mismatch is documented, medium is the safest choice under uncertainty.
conditions: IF account data or media subject to retention limits is uploaded, policy obligations apply.
IF EU/regulated content is routed through social-auto-upload to a non-compliant destination, a breach may occur.
mitigations: Confirm the destination platform’s retention policy.
Avoid uploading regulated content.
Limit account credentials to the minimum needed.
Review logs for stored personal data.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and retention controls.
